title: core
text:
Searching
A query can carry filters as key:value tokens next to the words, as in merge dicts package:fastcore path:basics. parseq splits a query into the plain text and a dict of filters. The keys are file, path, package, lang and type, and the short forms people tend to type first also work: pkg, dir, folder, ext, plurals such as packages, and so on. A value can list several options separated by commas. A trailing !, as in package!:fastcore, is accepted and means the same as without it, because every filter already excludes everything that does not match. A token that looks like a filter but has an unknown key, such as libr:litesearch, is reported under _unknown, so a caller can warn about it instead of silently searching for the literal text. If a query holds nothing but filters, the whole query is kept as the search text.



parseq
def parseq(
    q:str
)->tuple:
Split query q into its plain text and a dict of key:value filters, with unknown keys under _unknown.



# aliases and the `!` suffix resolve to the canonical key
for tok in ['package:litesearch', 'pkg:litesearch', 'pkgs:litesearch', 'package!:litesearch', 'pkg!:litesearch']:
    raw, fs = parseq(f'how do I add indexes with {tok}')
    assert fs['package'] == ['litesearch'], (tok, dict(fs))
    assert raw == 'how do I add indexes with', (tok, raw)
assert parseq('atomic save dir:xtras')[1]['path'] == ['xtras']
assert parseq('atomic save ext:py')[1]['lang'] == ['py']
assert parseq('search package:httpx,requests')[1]['package'] == ['httpx', 'requests']

# an unknown filter key is reported, not silently searched as text
assert parseq('add indexes with libr:litesearch')[1]['_unknown'] == ['libr']
assert parseq('add indexes with module:foo')[1]['_unknown'] == ['module']
# ...and known keys, urls and bare prose never trip it
for q in ['add indexes with package:litesearch', 'see https://example.com/x', 'how do I add indexes']:
    assert '_unknown' not in parseq(q)[1], q


parseq('how do I merge dicts package:fastcore path:data*')

('how do I merge dicts',
 defaultdict(list, {'package': ['fastcore'], 'path': ['data*']}))



assert parseq('stripe payments package:fasthtml file:routes*') == ('stripe payments', {'package': ['fasthtml'], 'file': ['routes*']})
assert parseq('package:monsterui package:fasthtml create a table') == ('create a table', {'package': ['monsterui', 'fasthtml']})
assert parseq('no filters here') == ('no filters here', {})
assert parseq('type:FunctionDef lang:py') == ('type:FunctionDef lang:py', {'type': ['FunctionDef'], 'lang': ['py']})
assert parseq('package:only')[0] == 'package:only'
# plural forms + comma-separated values
assert parseq('merge dicts packages:fastcore,litesearch') == ('merge dicts', {'package': ['fastcore', 'litesearch']})
assert parseq('search paths:basics,core,data') == ('search', {'path': ['basics', 'core', 'data']})
assert parseq('query packages:fastcore,litesearch paths:basics,core') == ('query', {'package': ['fastcore', 'litesearch'], 'path': ['basics', 'core']})
assert parseq('langs:py,js files:routes*,api*') == ('langs:py,js files:routes*,api*', {'lang': ['py', 'js'], 'file': ['routes*', 'api*']})
print('parse_query: all assertions pass')

parse_query: all assertions pass



from litesearch import pre, clean


assert clean('with_uv') == 'with_uv'

filt2wh turns those filters into an SQL WHERE clause for one of the two indexes. file and path values are globs (* and ?) matched anywhere in the path. lang takes an extension or a language name (py or python). type matches the chunk’s syntax type, such as FunctionDef or ClassDef. package applies only to the package index, so on the repo index a filter dict holding only a package gives None, meaning no filter.



filt2wh
def filt2wh(
    filters:dict, store:str='code'
)->str | None:
An SQL WHERE clause for filters (from parseq) on the code or env store, or None if nothing applies.





sql_str
def sql_str(
    v
)->str:
v as an SQLite string literal: single-quoted, with each internal quote doubled.



# a `lang:` filter is answered from idx_store_lang on both stores, not by reading every row's metadata JSON
for _db, _s in ((k.codedb, 'code'), (k.envdb, 'env')):
    _plan = ' '.join(r['detail'] for r in _db.q(f"explain query plan select rowid from store where {filt2wh(parseq('x lang:rs')[1], _s)}"))
    assert 'idx_store_lang' in _plan, _plan


filt2wh(parseq('how do I merge dicts package:fastcore path:data*')[1], 'env')

"(json_extract(metadata, '$.path') like '%data%') AND (package='fastcore')"



filt2wh({'type': ['FunctionDef']}, 'code')

"(json_extract(metadata, '$.type') = 'FunctionDef')"



assert filt2wh({'file': ['routes*']}, 'code') == "(path LIKE '%routes%')"
assert filt2wh({'path': ['api/*']}, 'code') == "(path LIKE '%api/%')"
assert filt2wh({'lang': ['py']}, 'code') == "(json_extract(metadata, '$.lang') = '.py')"
assert filt2wh({'lang': ['python']}, 'code') == "(json_extract(metadata, '$.lang') = '.py')"
assert filt2wh({'package': ['fasthtml']}, 'env') == "(package='fasthtml')"
assert filt2wh({'type': ['FunctionDef']}, 'code') == "(json_extract(metadata, '$.type') = 'FunctionDef')"
assert filt2wh({}, 'code') is None
assert filt2wh({}, 'env') is None
assert filt2wh({'package': ['fasthtml']}, 'code') is None
print('filters_to_where: all assertions pass')

filters_to_where: all assertions pass


filt2wh quotes every filter value with sql_str. A value is always one SQL string literal, whatever quotes it holds. A value that holds a quote of either kind matches that literal text and never changes the clause. sql_str raises ValueError for a value that holds a NUL character. Ordinary values give the same text as before.

import sqlite3
from fastcore.test import expect_fail


_qdb = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
_qdb.execute('create table store(package text, metadata text, path text)')
_qdb.executemany('insert into store values (?, ?, ?)', [('x', '{}', 'a.py'), ('y', '{}', 'b.py')])
_qrows = lambda fs: [r[0] for r in _qdb.execute(f"select package from store where {filt2wh(fs, 'env')}")]
_qodd = ['x"\' OR 1=1 --', "it's", parseq('q package:x"\' OR 1=1 --')[1]['package'][0]]
test_eq([_qrows({'package': [v]}) for v in _qodd], [[], [], []])
test_eq(_qrows({'package': ['x']}), ['x'])
test_eq(filt2wh({'package': ['x', 'y']}, 'env'), "(package='x' OR package='y')")
with expect_fail(ValueError, contains='NUL'): sql_str('a\x00b')
filt2wh({'package': [_qodd[0]]}, 'env')

env_context searches the package index and repo_context searches the repo index. Each parses the filters, embeds the query, runs one search that combines keyword and vector matching, and returns hits with their content and metadata. Use one of them when you know which index you want. Kosha.context, defined in the graph module, searches both indexes, reranks the hits for code and adds call-graph details. Use Kosha.context by default.
Both take limit, an extra SQL where, and rerank=True to reorder the hits with a flashrank cross-encoder, a small model that scores each hit against the query. When reranking, kosha first retrieves a wider pool of candidates (fanout) for the reranker to choose from. It then cuts the result to limit. pkgs2consider returns the names of indexed packages, or with sys_wide=False only those indexed at the version your project uses.



Kosha.pkgs2consider
def pkgs2consider(
    sys_wide:bool=True
)->set:
Names of indexed packages, or with sys_wide=False only those indexed at the installed version.





Kosha.env_context
def env_context(
    q:str, # query to search (supports key:value filters)
    emb_q:str=None, # query to embed; defaults to bare query after filter parsing
    columns:str='content,metadata,package', # comma separated columns string to return from search
    where:str=None, # additional where clause to filter search results
    ann:bool=True, # HNSW Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ann) search; defaults to True
    rerank:bool=False, # reorder the merged hits with a flashrank cross-encoder
    rerank_model:str=None, # flashrank model name (None -> fast default)
    **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L: # additional args to pass to db.search
Keyword and vector search over the package index, with optional key:value filters.





fanout
def fanout(
    kw, limit, rerank
):
Set the retrieval limit in kw, widened to at least RERANK_FANOUT when reranking.



# `sys_wide=False` keeps a package indexed at the installed version, also when the index holds two versions of it
from types import SimpleNamespace
_fk = SimpleNamespace(env_path=None, root=None, pkgs=lambda select: [dict(name='a', version='1'), dict(name='b', version='1'), dict(name='b', version='2')])
_epv, env_pkg_versions = env_pkg_versions, lambda path=None, root=None: {'a': '1', 'b': '2', 'c': '1'}
try:
    test_eq(Kosha.pkgs2consider(_fk, sys_wide=False), {'a', 'b'})
    test_eq(set(Kosha.pkgs2consider(_fk)), {'a', 'b'})
finally: env_pkg_versions = _epv




Kosha.watch_repo
def watch_repo(
    dir:pathlib.Path=None, **kw
):
Watch the repo and re-index files as they change, until you press Ctrl-C.





Kosha.awatch_repo
async def awatch_repo(
    dir:pathlib.Path=None, **kw
):
Watch dir asynchronously and re-index the files in each change event.





Kosha.repo_context
def repo_context(
    q:str, # query to search (supports key:value filters)
    emb_q:str=None, # query to embed; defaults to bare query after filter parsing
    columns:str='content,path,metadata', # columns to return
    where:str=None, # extra SQL filter
    ann:bool=True, # HNSW Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ann) search; defaults to True
    rerank:bool=False, # reorder the merged hits with a flashrank cross-encoder
    rerank_model:str=None, # flashrank model name (None -> fast default)
    **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L: # additional args to pass to db.search
Keyword and vector search over the repo index, with optional key:value filters.



import inspect


# `wide` was accepted and ignored; the FTS leg always ORs the query terms through litesearch's `pre`.
assert 'wide' not in inspect.signature(Kosha.env_context).parameters
assert 'wide' not in inspect.signature(Kosha.repo_context).parameters

watch_repo keeps the repo index current while you work. It blocks and watches the repository with watchfiles. After every change it calls update_repo with the changed files. It runs until you press Ctrl-C. awatch_repo is the same loop as a coroutine, for code that already runs an event loop.

title: core
text:
One row shape
A tool that shows kosha hits next to hits from other sources, such as documentation or notes, needs every hit in one format. code_row turns one hit from repo_context or env_context into an AttrDict with six keys: source (which index the hit came from), ref (the dotted name, or the path), title, where (path:line), text (the first 600 characters of the chunk) and open. open is a hint for how to open the hit, such as symbol('pkg.mod'). rows runs the searches and returns the hits in that format. It searches the repo index by default. Pass env=True to add the package index.



Kosha.rows
def rows(
    q:str, # query, with kosha's key:value filters
    limit:int=12, repo:bool=True, # the repo index
    env:bool=False, # the installed-package index
    **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L: # forwarded to repo_context / env_context
Search hits for q from the repo and, with env=True, the package index, each as a code_row.





code_row
def code_row(
    r:dict, # a hit from `repo_context` or `env_context`
    leg:str='repo', # which index it came from
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Hit r as an AttrDict with the keys source, ref, title, where, text and open.


pkg_context searches package descriptions, the records pkg_doc builds, to find a package by what it does. It reads the pkg_store table, which update_pkg fills with one record per package through put_pkg_doc.



Kosha.pkg_context
def pkg_context(
    q:str, # the search query
    limit:int=10, # number of hits to return
    rerank:bool=False, # reorder the merged hits with a flashrank cross-encoder
    rerank_model:str=None, # flashrank model name (None -> fast default)
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Keyword and vector search over the package descriptions in pkg_store.



# update_pkg fills pkg_store with one description per package; reindexing replaces it rather than adding another.
_pt = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _pkk = Kosha(dir=_pt, xdg_dir=_pt)
_pkk.update_pkg('certifi', verbose=False); _pkk.update_pkg('certifi', verbose=False, force=True)
assert len(_pkk.pkg_st()) == 1
_r = _pkk.pkg_context('Mozilla CA bundle certificates', limit=3)
assert _r and _r[0]['metadata']['name'] == 'certifi', _r


# `cast_emb` pins the stored dtype to what `Database.search` reads back (float16), so a
# custom `efn` emitting float32 can no longer corrupt the vector leg silently.
emb = k.emb_doc(['def f(): pass'])
qry = k.emb_query('a function')
assert emb.dtype == DTYPE == np.float16, emb.dtype
assert qry.dtype == DTYPE, qry.dtype

f32 = cast_emb(lambda txts, **kw: np.zeros((len(txts), 4), dtype=np.float32))
assert f32(['a','b']).dtype == DTYPE


# rerank fans out to RERANK_FANOUT candidates, then the cross-encoder cuts back to `limit`.
assert fanout({}, 5, True)['limit'] == RERANK_FANOUT
assert fanout({}, 50, True)['limit'] == 50
assert fanout({}, 5, False)['limit'] == 5

# the live leg needs flashrank's model on disk; skip rather than fail on a cold/offline machine.
try: rr = k.env_context('atomic file write', limit=5, rerank=True)
except Exception as e: print('rerank skipped:', type(e).__name__)
else:
    assert len(rr) <= 5
    wide = k.env_context('atomic file write', limit=RERANK_FANOUT)
    assert {r['content'] for r in rr} <= {r['content'] for r in wide}, 'reranked hits must come from the fanout'
    print(rr.attrgot('metadata').attrgot('mod_name'))

title: core
text:
Docs index
Code chunks suit code, but a README or a docs/ folder reads better as whole sections. kosha keeps a third index for such prose, built on litesearch’s Index, which splits documents by their headings and can search, list and return whole sections. It lives in the shared data directory (docs.db), next to the package index, and is created the first time you use it.
add_docs adds a folder of documents, a single file, or a dict of {title: text}, and returns the number of chunks added. add_pkg_docs adds a package’s full README. docs_context searches the docs index. By default it returns ranked sections, each with a node_id you can pass to k.docs.read to get the whole section; sections=False returns the raw chunks. The docs index uses the same embedding model as the code indexes, so only one model is loaded.



Kosha.docs_context
def docs_context(
    q:str, # the search query
    limit:int=5, # hits to return
    sections:bool=True, # ranked sections (with `read` handles) vs raw chunks
    **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L: # forwarded to Index.sections / Index.search
Search the docs index, returning whole sections by default or raw chunks with sections=False.





Kosha.add_pkg_docs
def add_pkg_docs(
    pkg:str
)->int:
Add the full README of installed package pkg to the docs index.





Kosha.add_docs
def add_docs(
    src, # a docs directory, a file, or {title: text}
    **kw
)->int: # forwarded to Index.add
Add documents to the docs index and return the number of chunks added.





Kosha.docs
def docs()->litesearch.api.Index:
The docs index, a litesearch Index over READMEs and other prose, opened on first use.



from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

with TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    _dk = Kosha(dir=Path(td), xdg_dir=Path(td))
    n = _dk.add_docs({'install': '# Install

Run `uv add kosha` to install kosha into your project.',
                    'search':  '# Search

Call `env_context` to search installed packages by meaning.'})
    assert n > 0, 'docs index ingested nothing'
    assert len(_dk.docs) == n
    hits = _dk.docs_context('how do I install this', sections=False)
    assert hits, 'no docs hits'
    assert 'uv add kosha' in hits[0]['content']
    secs = _dk.docs_context('search installed packages')
    assert secs and _dk.docs.read(secs[0]['node_id'])['text']
    print(repr(_dk.docs))

text:
Keeping syncs fast
Indexing is meant to fit in an edit and search loop. Repo and package updates touch only what changed. The call graph is optional, and sync(graph=False) skips it when you need only search. The default graph update reads changed Python files in one fast pass. The slower full extraction runs only with graph_mode='full'. PageRank is recomputed only when the number of edges has changed by more than 10%. graph_metrics=False stops the recomputation.

title: graph
text:
Edges come from two passes over the source. The static pass uses ast-grep to find every place a function, class or method is named inside another and binds that name to its definition. The dynamic pass uses Python’s ast module to find dependencies that are not written as calls, such as decorators and handler tables.
CodeGraph holds the graph in one SQLite database. Pass a file path, or ':memory:' for a throwaway graph. It has six tables.
Kosha.graph opens the CodeGraph for your repository. You rarely build one yourself. The examples below use an empty in-memory graph.
CodeGraph
def CodeGraph(
    path:str | pathlib.Path=':memory:', busy_timeout:int=None, # ms to wait for a locked database
):
A call graph of Python code, stored in SQLite, with methods to build and query it.
cg = CodeGraph(':memory:')
tables = {r[0] for r in cg.db.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")}

print("schema ok:", tables)

title: graph
text:
Dynamic edges
Some dependencies are never written as calls. A web framework calls hello because @app.route('/hello') registered it. The fastcore @patch decorator adds a plain function to a class as a method. dyn_edges reads the source of one module and returns these dependencies as edges. It finds six kinds:

decorator: @app.route(...) above def hello gives an edge from app to hello. The decorator must be an attribute of a name, such as app.route. Confidence is 0.95 when app comes from a known web framework: fasthtml, flask, fastapi, starlette, django, aiohttp, sanic, tornado, litestar or blacksheep. Otherwise confidence is 0.75 when the method name is a registration verb, and 0.5 for any other name. The registration verbs are add, register, include, on, connect, mount, sub, subscribe, listen, use, route, handle, hook, attach, bind, plug, get, post, put, delete, patch, head, options, before, after and middleware. A verb can have a suffix, as in add_route. Case does not matter.
registration: a call such as app.register(hello) gives an edge from app to hello. The method name must be a registration verb, and hello must be a function defined in the module. Confidence follows the same rule as decorator.
connect_body: a function named connect, setup, register, init_app, create_app, mount, configure, bootstrap, install or activate gives edges when its body passes a plain name to a method of its first parameter. Each edge runs from the function to the passed name. Confidence is 0.9.
patch: @patch def f(self:Table) gives an edge from Table to f. An annotation such as Table|View gives one edge for each class. Confidence is 0.9.
delegates: @delegates(target) on wrapper gives an edge from wrapper to target. Confidence is 0.85.
co_dispatch: a module-level list, tuple or dict of the module’s functions, such as HANDLERS = [a, b, c], makes those functions peers. For a dict, the values are the functions. Confidence is 0.8. The peers of a handler show the pattern to follow when you add a new handler. CodeGraph stores peers as groups in the co_dispatch table, not as edges.

The examples below show each kind.



dyn_edges
def dyn_edges(
    src:str, module:str
)->list[dict]:
Edges from decorators, registration calls, setup functions, @patch, @delegates and handler tables in src, with nodes named under module.


A call like self.db.search(q) names a method, search, on an object whose type the source does not state. Kosha can resolve the call only when it knows which search methods exist. While it reads a module, Kosha records one hint for each such call inside an indexed function. A hint holds the calling function, the method name and the packages the module imports, in import order. resolve_attr_calls turns the hints into edges later. A module that imports nothing gives hints that never resolve.

from fastcore.test import test_eq


_src = "from litesearch import *\ndef f(self): self.db.search(q)\ndef g(self): self.st.insert(x)"
_meta = {'m.f': {}, 'm.g': {}}
_hints = _attr_call_hints(sources={'m': _src}, meta=_meta)
test_eq(len(_hints), 2)
test_eq({h['method'] for h in _hints}, {'search','insert'})
assert all('litesearch' in h['pkgs'].split(',') for h in _hints)
# a function missing from `meta` gives no hint
test_eq(_attr_call_hints(sources={'m': _src}, meta={}), [])
# `self.method()` and calls on other objects give no hint
_src2 = "def f(self): self.direct(); other.thing()"
test_eq(_attr_call_hints(sources={'m2': _src2}, meta={'m2.f':{}}), [])

src="""
def f(self):
    self.db.search(q)
    self.store.insert(x)
    self.direct()        # depth 1 — skip
    other.thing()        # not self — skip
"""
_fn = [n for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(_src)) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef)]
test_eq(_attr_calls(_fn[0]), {'search'})
test_eq(_attr_calls(_fn[1]), {'insert'})

In this Flask snippet, @app.route produces a decorator edge from mymod.app to mymod.hello. The call other_app.register(hello) produces a registration edge from mymod.other_app to mymod.hello. A function with at least one parameter and one of these names also produces connect_body edges: connect, setup, register, init_app, create_app, mount, configure, bootstrap, install, activate. These edges run from the function to each plain name that the function passes to a method of its first parameter. Here setup produces a connect_body edge from mymod.setup to mymod.hello. A registration edge needs the argument to be a function defined in the same module. Source that does not parse produces no edges. The two cells after this one show the delegates and patch kinds.

_SRC = '''
import flask
app = flask.Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/hello')
def hello(): pass

def setup(other_app):
    other_app.register(hello)
'''

kinds = {e['kind'] for e in edges}
assert 'decorator' in kinds, f"Expected decorator edge, got: {edges}"
assert 'registration' in kinds, f"Expected registration edge, got: {edges}"
assert dyn_edges('def (broken', 'bad') == L()
print("_dyn_edges ok:", edges)

  'callee': 'mymod.target',

resolve_attr_calls turns the pending hints into attr_call edges with confidence 0.7. For each hint it finds the graph nodes whose last name is the method and whose package the calling module imports. It picks the node from the package that the module imports last. It adds no edge when the caller already has an edge to that node. from_sources, from_dir, from_pkg and sync call it at the end of a build. The tests further down call it on hints inserted by hand.



CodeGraph.resolve_attr_calls
def resolve_attr_calls()->CodeGraph:
Turn pending self.x.method() hints into attr_call edges, now that the graph knows which methods exist.

title: graph
text:
Static edges
static_edges reads source with ast-grep. It returns a list of edges and a dict of node metadata keyed by node name. Every edge has kind static and confidence 1.0. The metadata holds the flavor (function, class or method), the file and the short method name. Pass either sources, a dict of {module name: source text}, or filenames with the root directory that module names are relative to. Without root, static_edges uses the parent of the first file’s folder. Passing both sources and filenames, or neither, raises AssertionError.
An edge means that the caller uses the callee by name. A call helper() counts. Passing helper as a value also counts. Kosha looks for the definition of a name in three places, in this order:

A definition in an enclosing scope: the function, its class or the module.
The module’s imports. The edge points to the imported name, even when the corpus does not define it.
The only definition with that name in the whole corpus.

Kosha makes no edge when none of the three applies. Three further rules limit the edges. Kosha reads an attribute only when it is reached through self, and it resolves self.m in step 1 only. An attribute on any other object, such as x.get, makes no edge, because x.get() could call the get of any object. Step 3 never applies to a name that is a Python builtin, such as list. A name that appears only in an import statement makes no edge.
The first example graphs two lines of source. A file that does not parse gives no edges and no nodes.



static_edges
def static_edges(
    sources:dict[str, str]=None, filenames:list[str]=None, root:str=None
)->tuple[list[dict], dict]:
Call edges and node metadata for sources ({module: source}) or for filenames under root, read with ast-grep.

meta['mod.foo']

{'node': 'mod.foo', 'flavor': 'function', 'file': '', 'method': 'foo'}

title: graph
text:
Building a graph
Every node has three numbers. in_degree is the number of edges into the node, which is its number of callers. out_degree is the number of edges out of the node, which is its number of callees. pagerank is the score from the PageRank algorithm, which Google first used to rank web pages. A node has a high score when many nodes depend on it, or when heavily used nodes depend on it. Kosha uses the score as a measure of reach. A change to a node with a high PageRank affects more code.
Kosha refreshes degrees after every update. PageRank is slow on a large graph. Kosha recomputes it when no PageRank has run yet, or when the number of edges has changed by more than 10% since the last run.
from_sources builds a graph from a dict of {module name: source text}. Use it to try the graph on a snippet. It also records each module-level name bound to a lambda, or to a partial, bind or curry call, as a function node.



CodeGraph.from_sources
def from_sources(
    sources:dict[str, str], chunk_size:int=50
):
Build the graph from a dict of {module name: source text}.

title: graph
text:
Querying the graph
All queries take full node names. callers(n) and callees(n) return the nodes one edge away, and with_kind=True returns (name, kind) pairs instead. neighbors(n, depth) returns every node within depth edges in either direction.
co_dispatched(node) returns the other members of the node’s co-dispatch group: the functions it shares a route list or handler table with. ranked(k, module) returns the k nodes with the highest PageRank, optionally only those under a module prefix.
short_path(src, tgt) follows edges from caller to callee and returns the shortest chain from src to tgt, or an empty list when there is none. short_paths(nodes, k) does this for every pair among the first k nodes and returns the paths longest first. edge_kinds() counts the edges of each kind.
Call node_info(node) before you change a function. It returns the node’s row from graph_nodes together with its callers, callees and co-dispatch peers. node_infos returns the same records for many nodes with one query per table. Kosha.context uses node_infos to annotate search hits.



CodeGraph.node_info
def node_info(
    node:str, # fully-qualified node name
    with_kind:bool=False, # include edge kind in callers/callees tuples
)->dict:
The graph_nodes row for node plus its callers, callees and co-dispatch peers.





CodeGraph.edge_kinds
def edge_kinds()->dict:
Count of each edge kind in the graph (static, decorator, patch, registration, etc.).





CodeGraph.short_paths
def short_paths(
    nodes, # iterable of fully-qualified node names
    k:int=10, # consider only the first k nodes
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Shortest paths between pairs among the first k of nodes, longest first.





CodeGraph.short_path
def short_path(
    src:str, # fully-qualified source node name
    tgt:str, # fully-qualified target node name
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Shortest chain of edges from src to tgt, or an empty L if there is none.





CodeGraph.ranked
def ranked(
    k:int=10, # number of top nodes to return
    module:str=None, # optional module prefix filter (e.g. 'fastcore.basics')
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
The k nodes with the highest PageRank, optionally only those whose name starts with module and a dot.





CodeGraph.co_dispatched
def co_dispatched(
    node:str, # fully-qualified node name
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Nodes registered in the same dispatch group as node (route list, handler table, etc.).





CodeGraph.neighbors
def neighbors(
    n:str, # fully-qualified node name
    depth:int=1, # number of hops to expand
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Every node within depth edges of n, in either direction.

    n:str, # fully-qualified node name
    with_kind:bool=False, # if True, return (callee, edge_kind) tuples instead of plain names

text:
Public API
public_api(pkg) lists the public names of a package, or of a module within it. It reads both the package index and the repo index. A name is public when it is in the module’s __all__. In a module without __all__, a name is public when it has no leading underscore. The list also holds functions that fastcore’s @patch adds to a class. Kosha finds them through the graph’s patch edges.
The list has this order: the package itself, then top-level names before nested names such as methods, then alphabetical order. meta_cols is a comma-separated string of metadata fields. Each entry is a dict with one key per field. limit caps the number of entries.



Kosha.public_api
def public_api(
    pkg:str, # package or module name, such as `fastcore` or `fastcore.basics`
    meta_cols:str='mod_name,docstring', # comma-separated metadata fields to return for each name

title: graph
text:
Freshness
status reports how far the index has drifted from the code on disk. It returns a dict with these keys:

files: the number of repo files indexed.
packages: the number of indexed package versions.
graph_nodes: the number of nodes in the graph.
stale_files: the number of indexed repo files modified since they were indexed.
new_files: the number of Python files in the repo that are not indexed.
stale_pkgs: a dict of {name: version} for each installed package not indexed at its installed version.

The packages considered are those listed in pyproject.toml and their dependencies, depth levels down. A sync with no package list indexes the packages in stale_pkgs.



Kosha.status
def status(
    pyproject:bool=True, depth:int=1
)->dict:
How fresh the index is: counts of files, packages and graph nodes, plus stale files, new files and stale packages.


status reads the project’s environment too: stale_pkgs lists a dependency installed only in the project’s .venv, and drops it once update_pkg has indexed that copy.

_root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'proj'; (_root/'.git').mkdir(parents=True)
(_root/'pyproject.toml').write_text('[project]\nname = "proj"\nversion = "0"\ndependencies = ["kkfake"]\n')
_sp = _root/'.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages'; (_sp/'kkfake').mkdir(parents=True)
(_sp/'kkfake'/'__init__.py').write_text('def hello(): return 1\n')
(_sp/'kkfake-1.0.dist-info').mkdir()
(_sp/'kkfake-1.0.dist-info'/'METADATA').write_text('Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: kkfake\nVersion: 1.0\nAuthor-email: a@b.co\n')
_kp, _cwd = Kosha(dir=_root, xdg_dir=_root/'xdg'), os.getcwd()
os.chdir(_root)
try:
    _before = _kp.status()['stale_pkgs']
    _kp.update_pkg('kkfake', embed=False, verbose=False)
    _after = _kp.status()['stale_pkgs']
finally: os.chdir(_cwd)
test_eq(list(_before), ['kkfake'])
test_eq(_after, {})

status and sync take the dependencies from the pyproject.toml in Kosha.root, not from the repository around the current folder. A server whose working folder is elsewhere, or inside another repository, still indexes the packages of the Kosha(dir=...) it was given. The next cell runs from repository a against a Kosha on b, which has no .git of its own.

title: graph
text:
Ranking
A search returns candidates from two lists, the repo index and the package index. Kosha merges the lists with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF). Each candidate scores 1/(k + rank) for every list that holds it. That order does not use the structure of code. rank_results adjusts the scores with rules adapted from the semble code-search library. In the table, top is the highest score among the candidates.








Rule
Condition
Effect on the score




1
is_symbol_query is true and the chunk defines the symbol, as in def Client, class Client or CREATE TABLE Client
Add 3.0 x top. Add 4.5 x top when the file name also matches the symbol.


2a
The query is natural language and the file or folder name matches at least 10% of its words
Add top x the share of words matched


2b
The query is natural language and names a CamelCase symbol that the chunk defines
Add 1.5 x top, or 2.25 x top when the file name also matches


3
The chunk comes from a package that the query names
Multiply by 1.5


4
A file has several high-scoring chunks
Add up to 0.2 x top to the best chunk of the file, in proportion to the sum of the file’s scores


5a
The path is a test file or test folder, a compat, _compat or legacy folder, or an examples folder
Multiply by 0.3 for each of these that matches


5b
The file is __init__.py or package-info.java
Multiply by 0.5


5c
The file ends in .d.ts
Multiply by 0.7


6
The file already supplies a chunk to the result
Each further chunk from the file counts half as much as the one before it



is_symbol_query is true for a dotted, ::, -> or backslash-qualified name, a name with a leading underscore, a name with a capital letter or underscore after its first character, and a name that starts with a capital letter. Examples are Client, Sinatra::Base and _private. penalise_paths=False turns off rules 5a to 5c. Rule 6 stops one file from filling the results.



rank_results
def rank_results(
    results, query, soft_pkgs:NoneType=None, top_k:NoneType=None, penalise_paths:bool=True
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Reorder search hits for code: symbol and file-name boosts, package boosts, and penalties for tests and repeated files.





is_symbol_query
def is_symbol_query(
    query:str
)->bool:
True if the query looks like a bare symbol or namespace-qualified identifier.



from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail

# is_symbol_query: symbols vs NL
for s in ['Client','Sinatra::Base','_private','StateManager','foo.bar']: assert is_symbol_query(s), s
for s in ['session','merge dicts','extract bytes from image']: assert not is_symbol_query(s), s

# path penalties: tests/__init__/examples/.d.ts penalised, plain source not
assert _file_penalty('kosha/core.py') == 1.0
assert _file_penalty('tests/test_core.py') < 1.0
assert _file_penalty('pkg/__init__.py') == _MODERATE_PENALTY
assert _file_penalty('examples/demo.py') == _STRONG_PENALTY
assert _file_penalty('types/foo.d.ts') == _MILD_PENALTY

def _r(content='x', path='a.py', pkg=None, rrf=0.01, **kw):
    md = {'path': path, 'package': pkg}
    return dict(content=content, metadata=md, path=path, _rrf_score=rrf, **kw)

# package boost: fastcore ranked above equal-base non-fastcore, but non-fastcore still present
res = [_r('a', 'other.py', pkg='numpy', rrf=0.01), _r('b', 'fc.py', pkg='fastcore', rrf=0.01)]
ranked = rank_results(res, 'extract bytes', soft_pkgs={'fastcore'})
test_eq(len(ranked), 2)
test_eq(_rk_pkg(ranked[0]), 'fastcore')

# empty / no-crash

title: graph
text:
Incremental sync
Re-reading a large environment takes minutes. Sync reads only the files whose content has changed. file_index stores a BLAKE2 hash of every analysed file. sync_dir compares the hashes, drops the nodes of deleted files and re-extracts changed files.
In the default mode='fast', sync_dir replaces the nodes and outgoing edges of a changed file. It keeps the edges from other files into that file. It removes edges into nodes that no longer exist. mode='full' re-extracts through process_files, which uses worker processes.
sync_pkgs runs sync_dir for the directory of each installed package. CodeGraph.sync runs sync_dir and sync_pkgs. If anything changed, it then updates degrees, and it updates PageRank when the edge count changed by more than 10%. metrics=False skips that step. Call recompute_metrics() once after several syncs. force=True re-reads every file.
This cell redefines _drop_file, _index_files, _stale and resolve_attr_calls from earlier in the notebook. The exported module contains the later versions.



CodeGraph.resolve_attr_calls
def resolve_attr_calls()->CodeGraph:
Turn pending self.x.method() hints into attr_call edges, now that the graph knows which methods exist.





CodeGraph.recompute_metrics
def recompute_metrics()->CodeGraph:
Recompute PageRank and degree metrics once after graph updates.





CodeGraph.sync
def sync(
    dir:NoneType=None, pkgs:NoneType=None, force:bool=False, mode:str='fast', metrics:bool=True, path:list=None
)->CodeGraph:
Update the graph for a directory and a list of packages. If anything changed and metrics is true, update degrees, and update PageRank when the edge count changed by more than 10%. force clears the pending method-call hints and reprocesses every file.





CodeGraph.sync_pkgs
def sync_pkgs(
    pkgs:list[str], force:bool=False, mode:str='fast', path:list=None
)->CodeGraph:
Update the graph for installed packages, skipping files whose content hash is unchanged.





CodeGraph.sync_dir
def sync_dir(
    dir:str | pathlib.Path, force:bool=False, mode:str='fast', root:NoneType=None
)->CodeGraph:
Update the graph for the .py files under dir. Skip files whose content hash is unchanged, and drop the rows of files that no longer exist. force reprocesses every file. mode="full" re-extracts changed files with process_files. root sets the module root.



from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from kosha.core import imp_root
with TemporaryDirectory() as _d:
    _sub = Path(_d)/'pkg'; _sub.mkdir()
    (_sub/'core.py').write_text('def helper(x): return x+1\ndef caller(x): return helper(helper(x))\n')
    (_sub/'other.py').write_text('from core import caller\ndef outer(): return caller(2)\n')
    _g2 = CodeGraph(':memory:').sync(dir=_d)
    _ids = {r['node'] for r in _g2.gn()}
    test_eq(imp_root(_sub/'core.py'), _sub)
    assert 'core.helper' in _ids and 'pkg.core.helper' not in _ids, sorted(_ids)
    test_eq(list(_g2.callers('core.helper')), ['core.caller'])

title: graph
text:
Syncing and searching from Kosha
Kosha.sync brings the repo index, the package index and the call graph up to date. It runs update_repo, update_pkgs and the graph sync in parallel threads. in_parallel=False runs them in turn. With no pkgs, it indexes the packages that status() reports as stale. repo, env and graph switch each part off. embed=False stores new chunks without vectors. Only keyword search finds them until process_repo or process_env adds the vectors. Kosha.sync returns the results of the three parts, not the Kosha.
Kosha.context is the default search. It runs repo_context and env_context in parallel and merges their hits with RRF. It reorders the hits with rank_results and keeps the top limit. With graph=True, the default, each hit also holds its graph record: pagerank, in_degree, out_degree, callers, callees and co_dispatched.
There are two ways to name a package in a query, and they differ. A package:fastcore filter skips the repo search and returns only code from fastcore. A package name written as a plain word, as in fastcore merge dicts, only boosts the chunks of that package. Chunks of other packages still appear.
compact=True returns slim dicts with mod_name, docstring, lineno, path and sig. sig is the first line of the chunk. rerank=True reorders the final hits with a flashrank cross-encoder. That needs the flashrank model on disk. The saved output below shows the step skipped on a machine without the model.



Kosha.context
def context(
    q:str, # query with optional key:value filters
    limit:int=50, repo:bool=True, env:bool=True, graph:bool=True, boost:bool=True,
    compact:bool=False, # return slim dicts (mod_name, docstring, lineno, path, sig) instead of full chunks
    columns:str='content,metadata', sys_wide:bool=True,
    rerank:bool=False, # reorder the boosted top-k with a flashrank cross-encoder
    rerank_model:str=None, # flashrank model name; None uses the fast default
    **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L: # forwarded to env_context / repo_context
Search the repo and the packages together, rerank the merged hits for code, and attach call-graph details.





Kosha.sync
def sync(
    pkgs:NoneType=None, # list of package names to sync (e.g. ['httpx', 'fastcore']); if None, sync every stale env package
    dir:NoneType=None, # directory to sync; if None, sync all of root
    verbose:bool=True, # print progress messages
    in_parallel:bool=True, # run the repo, package and graph updates in parallel threads; False runs them in turn
    graph_mode:str='fast', # 'full' re-extracts changed files in worker processes
    graph_metrics:bool=True, # refresh PageRank after the graph update; False leaves it for `k.graph.recompute_metrics()`
    force:bool=False, # reprocess every file and package, even unchanged ones, graph included
    repo:bool=True, # index the repo
    env:bool=True, # index installed packages; False indexes the repo only, even if `pkgs` is given
    graph:bool=True, # update the call graph
    sync_graph:NoneType=None, # deprecated: the old name for `graph`
    pyproject:bool=True, # if True, auto-detect env packages from the pyproject.toml in `Kosha.root` (not `dir`); if False, use pkgs argument as-is
    depth:int=1, # depth for pyproject env package detection; ignored if pyproject=False
    embed:bool=True, # compute vectors for new chunks; False stores them for keyword search only
    pkg_parallel:bool=False, # ingest env packages concurrently; requires Kosha(busy_timeout=...)
    chunk:int=5000, # rows per write transaction when pkg_parallel=True
)->Kosha:
Bring the repo index, the package index and the call graph up to date.

title: graph
text:
Package dependencies
When Kosha indexes a package, it counts which other packages the modules of that package import. It stores the counts in the pkg_deps table with the columns from_pkg, to_pkg and n_modules. dep_stack(seeds, depth) walks that table breadth first. Layer 0 is the seeds. Layer 1 is the packages that the seeds import, and so on, up to depth layers. With no_sys_pkg=True, the result keeps only names that are installed distributions (is_sys_pkg). allow restricts the result to a list of names. Use dep_stack to see what a package depends on before you read its code.
top_nodes(pkg, k) returns the k public names of a package with the highest PageRank, which are its most used entry points. api_call_paths(from_pkg, to_pkg, k) takes the top k nodes of each package. It returns {target: path} for the shortest call paths from the entry points of the first package to the entry points of the second. An empty dict, as in the fastlite example, means that no top node of the first package reaches a top node of the second.



Kosha.api_call_paths
def api_call_paths(
    from_pkg:str, # package whose public API is the call source
    to_pkg:str, # package whose public API is the call target
    k:int=15, # top-k API nodes per package to consider
)->dict:
Shortest call-graph paths from from_pkg public API nodes to to_pkg public API nodes.





Kosha.top_nodes
def top_nodes(
    pkg:str, k:int=5
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
The k public API nodes of pkg with the highest PageRank in the code graph.

text:
Where to add code
where_to_add(description) suggests where to put new code. It runs context on the description. For each hit in the repo index it returns a dict with node, path, insert_after, co_dispatched and pagerank. insert_after is the last line of the hit, or the last line of its last co-dispatch peer in the same file. Hits from installed packages are skipped because they are not in your repo. limit and other keyword arguments go to context.



Kosha.where_to_add
def where_to_add(
    description:str, limit:int=5, *, repo:bool=True, env:bool=True, graph:bool=True, boost:bool=True,
    compact:bool=False, columns:str='content,metadata', sys_wide:bool=True, rerank:bool=False, rerank_model:str=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Places to add code for description: the file, the line to insert after, and the peers it would join.



pts = k.where_to_add('add a new way to search codebase', limit=3)
assert isinstance(pts, L)
if pts:
    assert all(k in pts[0] for k in ('node','path','insert_after','co_dispatched','pagerank'))
    print('where_to_add ok:', pts[0]['path'], 'line', pts[0]['insert_after'])
else: print('where_to_add ok: no results (index may be empty)')

The next cell tests the incremental sync. Nested functions keep their own calls. Unchanged files are skipped. Removed definitions disappear. A caller-supplied root keeps the package name in node names.

from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

# Fast mode preserves lexical scope and does not attribute nested calls to the parent.
_src = '''
def target(): pass
class A:
    def same(self): target()
class B:
    def same(self): target()
def outer():
    def inner(): target()
    return inner
'''
_edges, _meta = static_edges({'m': _src})
_edge_pairs = {(e['caller'], e['callee']) for e in _edges}
assert {'m.A.same', 'm.B.same', 'm.outer', 'm.outer.inner'} <= set(_meta)
assert ('m.outer', 'm.target') not in _edge_pairs
assert {('m.A.same', 'm.target'), ('m.B.same', 'm.target'), ('m.outer.inner', 'm.target')} <= _edge_pairs

# Incremental fast sync records lambda ownership, skips unchanged source, and drops removed nodes.
with TemporaryDirectory() as _tmp:
    _path = Path(_tmp) / 'm.py'
    _path.write_text('x = lambda: 1\ndef keep(): return x()\ndef gone(): pass\n')
    _g = CodeGraph(':memory:').sync_dir(_tmp)
    _hash = _g.fi(where='path=?', where_args=[str(_path)])[0]['source_hash']
    _g.sync_dir(_tmp)
    assert _g.fi(where='path=?', where_args=[str(_path)])[0]['source_hash'] == _hash
    assert _g.gn(where='node=?', where_args=['m.x'])[0]['file'] == str(_path)
    _path.write_text('x = lambda: 2\ndef keep(): return x()\n')
    _g.sync_dir(_tmp)
    assert not _g.gn(where='node=?', where_args=['m.gone'])
    assert _g.gn(where='node=?', where_args=['m.x'])[0]['file'] == str(_path)

# Full mode replaces a changed file rather than retaining definitions removed from it.
with TemporaryDirectory() as _tmp:
    _path = Path(_tmp) / 'm.py'
    _path.write_text('def old(): pass\n')
    _g = CodeGraph(':memory:').sync_dir(_tmp, mode='full')
    _path.write_text('def new(): pass\n')
    _g.sync_dir(_tmp, mode='full')
    _nodes = set(L(_g.gn(select='node')).attrgot('node'))
    assert 'm.old' not in _nodes and 'm.new' in _nodes

# A caller-supplied root preserves the package segment in generated node names.
with TemporaryDirectory() as _tmp:
    _root, _pkg = Path(_tmp), Path(_tmp) / 'mypkg'
    _pkg.mkdir()
    (_pkg / 'core.py').write_text('def api(): pass\n')
    _g = CodeGraph(':memory:').sync_dir(_pkg, root=_root)
    assert _g.gn(where='node=?', where_args=['mypkg.core.api'])

# A file edited after it was parsed is recorded under the hash that was compared, so the next sync parses it again.
with TemporaryDirectory() as _tmp:
    _path = Path(_tmp) / 'm.py'
    _path.write_text('def a(): pass\n')
    _fp, _g = CodeGraph._fast_process_files, CodeGraph(':memory:')
    CodeGraph._fast_process_files = lambda self, *a, **k: (_fp(self, *a, **k), _path.write_text('def b(): pass\n'))[0]
    try: _g.sync_dir(_tmp)
    finally: CodeGraph._fast_process_files = _fp
    _g.sync_dir(_tmp)
    assert {r['node'] for r in _g.gn()} == {'m.b'}

# The busy timeout of a Kosha reaches its call graph, so concurrent writers wait for each other.
with TemporaryDirectory() as _tmp:
    _k = Kosha(dir=Path(_tmp), xdg_dir=Path(_tmp), busy_timeout=4321)
    assert _k.graph.db.q('pragma busy_timeout')[0]['timeout'] == 4321
    assert CodeGraph(Path(_tmp)/'g.db', busy_timeout=1234).db.q('pragma busy_timeout')[0]['timeout'] == 1234

# A node that loses its last edge goes back to degree zero.
_g = CodeGraph(':memory:')
_g.gn.insert_all([{'node': 'a'}, {'node': 'b'}])
_g.ge.insert({'caller': 'a', 'callee': 'b', 'kind': 'static', 'confidence': 1.0})
_g._centrality(); _g.ge.delete_where(); _g._centrality()
assert all(not r['in_degree'] and not r['out_degree'] for r in _g.gn())

print('fast incremental graph tests passed')

title: mcp
text:
The tools call the same Kosha methods as the command line and the daemon. The mcp package is a dependency of kosha, and nothing extra needs installing. kosha indexes the repository it starts in and that repository’s environment. Start the server at the project root, inside the project’s environment. uv run does both:
The server creates one Kosha on the first tool call and keeps it. The embedding model loads once per server and not once per call. The server converts results to plain JSON types before it returns them.

text:
Connect a client
The server must start at the project root inside the project’s environment. Use uv run kosha-mcp. uvx kosha-mcp runs the server in a separate environment that does not have your project’s packages.
For Claude Code, run this inside the project:
claude mcp add kosha -- uv run kosha-mcp
For Codex, add this to ~/.codex/config.toml. Codex starts servers in your session’s working directory. Start Codex at the project root.
[mcp_servers.kosha]
command = "uv"
args = ["run", "kosha-mcp"]
Claude Desktop does not start in your project. Name the project in claude_desktop_config.json:
{"mcpServers": {"kosha": {"command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--project", "/path/to/your/repo", "kosha-mcp"]}}}
